name: Elah
overview: Elah was a male chief of the Edomites, a people descended from Esau. He held a position of leadership within the Edomite tribe, as noted in Genesis 36:41. The biblical text identifies him specifically by his tribal affiliation and role, without additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Elah means 'species of a mighty tree,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as recorded in Genesis 36:41. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a strong, natural imagery consistent with biblical naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Elah is identified as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family relationships or details about his immediate relatives.
scriptureSignificance: Elah's significance lies in his role as a chief among the Edomites, a people closely related to Israel through Esau. His mention in the genealogical records of Genesis 36 highlights the established leadership and organization within Edom following Esau's descendants. This underscores the fulfillment of God's promise to Esau regarding his progeny and their prominence among neighboring nations.
